Dark redesign

Rendered from the redesigned 3D model, from about the same spots your photos were taken. The mahogany cupboards, grey walls and beige floor tiles stay exactly as they are. All the darkness comes from furniture, textiles and lighting.

Why it works

  • The cupboards are already a deep red-brown. Oxblood cushions and walnut wood repeat that tone, so the kitchen looks like part of the scheme rather than something you're stuck with.
  • You can't paint the light grey walls, so the dark mass sits low and in fabric: a charcoal rug, couch, bedding and floor-length curtains. Matte black metal adds the sharp lines.
  • Light makes the mood. Use warm 2700K bulbs in three or four low lamps, plus an LED strip under the upper cupboards, and leave the ceiling light off at night.
  • Curtains hung right up under the bulkhead hide the burglar bars and make the ceiling feel higher.

Layout and key pieces

  • Sleep zone by the big window: queen bed with a black upholstered headboard on the left wall, a black nightstand with a smoked-glass lamp, and a large black-framed print above.
  • Study nook on the same wall: black steel desk with a walnut top, two floating shelves and a desk lamp.
  • Lounge in the middle: charcoal 3 seater with its back to the bed (this zones the room), a black arc lamp, a round black coffee table, a walnut TV console and a 43 inch TV on the back wall, all on a 2.4 × 2 m charcoal rug.
  • Dining by the kitchen: round black table for two with a black dome pendant.
  • Kitchen: black fridge, microwave, kettle and toaster, a warm LED strip and one trailing plant on top of the cupboards.
  • Bathroom: black towels, mat and accessories against the white tiles, which picks up the black tile border.
